title: Skip the merge re-gate when the target has not moved since the daemon gate: gate() records the target and head it gated, merge() reuses that green result when the rebase was a no-op
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B9. Every merge runs the full gate again (merge.py gate.run_gate after the rebase)
even when the daemon gated the identical tree minutes earlier against the same target head; on luna-inbox the
Apple gate takes 9-11 min, so each task costs two gate runs.

Facts (goal/T-1403 at 92c1a98 plus T-1456 merged before this task; re-check line numbers):
- daemon.py:1396 gate(pool): runs gate.run_gate(worktree, script=merge.TESTS_GREEN, task_id, cfg) and on green
  stamps 'gated_at' (grep "stamp(t[\"id\"], \"gated_at\"" in gate()); it does not record which target sha or
  worktree head it gated.
- merge.py:28-122 merge(): rebase onto target (46), then gate.run_gate (62) unconditionally, then fast-forward.
  _diff_hash (11-21) and the reviewed_sha check already compare before/after rebase.
- gate.run_gate returns {'returncode', 'timed_out', 'stdout', 'stderr', ...} (gate.py).

Change:
1. daemon.gate(): on a green run, the gated_at stamp also writes pipeline.gated_target_sha = rev-parse of the
   merge target (goal/<parent>, or 'integration' without a parent, same rule as merge.py:30) and
   pipeline.gated_head = rev-parse HEAD of the worktree, both read through gitutil._git_in; a failed rev-parse
   leaves the keys absent.
2. merge.merge(): after the rebase, when pool config [merge].skip_regate_when_unmoved (default True; read via
   pool_config().get('merge', {}), import lazily like merge.py's other config reads) and
   pipeline.gated_target_sha == rev-parse(target) taken before the rebase and rev-parse HEAD of the worktree
   after the rebase == pipeline.gated_head: skip gate.run_gate, set result['gate'] = 'reused_green' and
   pipeline.merge_gate = {'mode': 'reused_green', 'gated_target_sha': ..., 'gated_head': ...}; otherwise run the
   gate as today and record pipeline.merge_gate = {'mode': 'ran'}. Never reuse when the task was held
   gate_timeout or gate_red after the stamp (the stamp is only written on green, and a later red clears
   gated_at via clear_stage, so check that gated_at is present).
3. orchestrator status / notify: one notify line '<id>: merge reused the daemon gate (target unmoved)' when
   reused.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_merge.py tests patch gate.run_gate and assert it was
called (grep 'run_gate' in tests/test_merge.py): those tasks have no gated_target_sha, so they keep running the
gate; tests/test_daemon.py gate tests assert the gated_at stamp (grep 'gated_at'): unchanged plus the two new keys.
Run tests/test_merge.py and tests/test_daemon.py.

Depends on B6 T-1456 (daemon.py and merge.py chain). Out of scope: gate.py, spawn.py.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never
background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py
like the neighbouring tests.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_gate_records_target_sha_and_head_on_green: passes: after a green daemon gate the task's pipeline holds gated_at, gated_target_sha equal to the goal branch head and gated_head equal to the worktree HEAD; a red gate writes neither

tests/test_merge.py::test_merge_reuses_daemon_gate_when_target_unmoved: passes: with gate.run_gate patched, merge.merge on a task whose pipeline.gated_target_sha equals the target head and whose rebase is a no-op does not call run_gate, merges, returns gate 'reused_green' and records pipeline.merge_gate mode 'reused_green'; when the target moved, when gated_head differs from HEAD after the rebase, when gated_at is absent, or when [merge].skip_regate_when_unmoved is False, run_gate is called as before
